known_archive_clock_anomaly.interpretation: Both roots have eight arrived outcomes with equal losses. The clock-reversing same-trip segment is an untraversed menu branch; the fixed executor would return service_or_clock_failure if it traversed that segment. It cannot create a strict positive root here.

post_audit_saved_trace_inspection.scope: Read-only inspection of the five differing saved journeys and two canceled initial endpoints; no control replay or sampled worlds.

cases.mechanism: Continue on IR36 to HB and transfer to S12; all six cheap policies alight at Oerlikon, take S21 to Hardbruecke and then S5.

Different S3/S6 incoming trips both alight at HB for the same IR36 430.TA.91-36-A-j23-1.142.H, cid188 (29421 to 29711). All six cheap policies continue to Hardbruecke and take the same S5 201.TA.91-5-C-j23-1.72.H, cid192 (29627 to 29794). Two entrance histories share one downstream competition event.
Continue on S20 to Hardbruecke and take S5; all six cheap policies alight at Stadelhofen and wait for S12.
Full/matched alight at HB and take S19; cheap/single/pair/one_step/CSA continue to Hardbruecke and take the faster S5. Mean also loses 172 seconds.

post_audit_saved_trace_inspection.conclusion: The four strict positive roots survive all six fixed cheap controls, but cover three dates and three downstream mechanism groups; roots98/99 share the same tail race. Both earlier and later alighting can help. The negative case, full-horizon missing-loss bounds and 49-second mean full-rollout CPU prevent treating these archive mechanisms as net value or G2. The canceled initial roots are common service failures, not archive clock artifacts or policy differences.
